items.note: Yellow header band with a sagging arc and a person-shaped cluster (crescent-shaded figure, an orange disc behind it, a star, a sparkle, a cloud) above a form on white. The errors use a red border plus an alert glyph and a message that says what to type. The invalid field that has focus shows only the blue focus border, so its error rests on the message alone; otherwise this is close to the reference's warm, flat craft.

A navy page with indigo inputs, a white selected nav pill and the yellow band kept at full strength, which matches the reference's night palette (03). The error messages are a readable coral. The focused invalid field again shows the yellow focus ring rather than a danger border.

The compact band keeps its cluster tucked into the top corner and the text wraps clear of it, as in the reference phone (04). The ink tab pill with its dot leads a scrolling tab strip. The errors are large and clear; the focused empty field shows blue, not red.

The same yellow profile band and form. The save result is a green tick and 'Saved' beside the ink save pill and the cream reset pill. It is clear but quiet, and it sits below the first screen. It is in the system's language but doesn't use the ink toast the spec offers for confirmations.
The night version keeps the yellow band, indigo fields and the white pill as primary. The saved state reads the same way as in light. The tone stacking is convincing against reference 03.

Full-width ink and cream pills stack in the form, with a green 'Saved' tick under them. The page rolls into the cream footer with a rising arc and an ink bottom bar. It is tidy and true to the reference's phone language.

A white radius-xl dialog with no shadow, a cream footer, a cream cancel pill and an ink confirm pill, set on a grey overlay over an orange billing band whose wallet-and-coin cluster pictures the area. Beneath it, the plan cards are now borderless cream with one violet selected plan and big bold prices, which closes the rc.3 pricing gap. The dialog is clear but plain; the reference shows no dialog to match.

The navy dialog has an indigo footer, an indigo cancel pill and a white confirm pill with an ink label, which follows the night role swap. The title and consequence copy are readable and say exactly what changes and when.

On the phone the dialog becomes a bottom sheet: bold title, close circle, full-width ink confirm over a cream cancel on a cream footer. It sits at the foot of the full-page capture because of how the page was captured. The sheet itself is well made, and the plan stack above it is borderless cream with a violet selected card.

Green security band with a crescent-shaded orange padlock, an ink shackle stroke, a yellow coin, a star and a cloud. A cream key plate opens the password group. Strength shows as a green dot. The mismatch message sits under the confirm field, but the field shows the blue focus border instead of red.

Night version: the green band and padlock scene are kept, and the indigo inputs have a yellow focus ring on the confirm field. Like the light version, the error is carried by the message only. The session table below stays undecorated.

The compact green band has its padlock cluster in the corner, and the key plate sits beside a bold group title. The 'Passwords do not match' message is clear, but the confirm field is blue (focused) rather than red. The selected tab pill is cut off at the right edge of the tab strip.

Focus on a sidebar nav item is a rounded blue pill ring offset from the item, which matches the reference's focus ring (11) and fixes the rc.3 square-box issue. The blue notifications band carries a crescent-shaded bell with a pink disc, a clapper, a star and a cloud. The cream group panel has an envelope plate and ink switches.

At night the focus ring turns yellow, still a rounded pill with an offset, and stands out well on the indigo sidebar. The white selected pill and the indigo panel with switches carry the night palette well.

The focused tab in the strip gets the rounded blue ring, but it is clipped at the screen's right edge because the strip doesn't scroll the focused tab into view. The compact blue band with its bell cluster and the cream email group are close to the reference.

The header cluster is a crescent-shaded blue figure with an orange disc behind its shoulder, a white star, a violet sparkle and a cloud. It pictures 'profile' plainly and spreads across about a third of the band. It is somewhat icon-like next to the reference's playful pieces (07), but built to the recipe. The other two crops are just band and footer arcs.

A tilted yellow bell with a darker crescent side, an orange clapper, a pink disc, a star and a cloud. The envelope and chat-bubble plates are distinct and fill most of their cream plates, each with a small sparkle. Each drawing reads as its subject, as in the reference's spot plates (07).

An orange padlock with a shaded side and keyhole, a fat ink shackle (the one allowed stroke), a yellow coin, a star and a cloud. The plates show a yellow key and a violet laptop, each its own silhouette. The laptop is flat with no crescent, so it is slightly plainer than the reference's pictograms.

A blue wallet with a darker clasp tab and a yellow coin rising out of it, plus a cloud, a star and a sparkle, which pictures billing well. The plates are rising yellow bars for plans, a card for payment and a green receipt for invoices: distinct and legible. The bars read more as statistics than as plans.

Settings group plates fade in once over 500ms with an ease-out curve, and the band art and form fields appear at once. No glyphs loop on these product screens, which matches the spec's calm reveal-once motion and the reference's restraint.

findings.summary: An invalid field that has focus shows only the focus border (blue by day, yellow at night) and drops the danger border, so the error is carried by the message under it alone. The spec gives focus and error each a border but never says which wins when both apply.
findings.promptFix: An invalid input keeps its 2px danger border while focused and shows focus with a 2px focus-ring outline offset 2px outside that border, so both states are visible at once.
findings.specRule: Inputs, selects | border → `color.text.secondary` | border → 2px `color.focus.ring` (the focus indicator; no outline, no glow) | — | error: 2px `color.status.danger` border

findings.summary: On phones the horizontal settings tab strip doesn't scroll the selected or focused tab into view. The tab pill and its focus ring are cut off at the right edge.
